intro: Professionals and everyday users convert psi (psi) to bars (bar) when working across imperial and metric standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One pounds per square inch equals 0.068948 bars, while 1 bar equals 14.503774 psi. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between psi and bar. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many bars (bar) are in 1 pounds per square inch (psi)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.06894757 bars (bar) in 1 pounds per square inch (psi), which rounds to 0.0689 bar for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 bar equals 14.503774 psi.

faqs.question: How do I convert psi to bars (psi to bar)?
faqs.answer: To convert psi to bars, use the formula: bar = psi × 0.06894757. For example, converting 32 psi gives 2.2063 bar.

faqs.question: What is 32 psi in bars?
faqs.answer: 32 psi (psi) equals exactly 2.2063 bars (bar) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
